issues.description: The detailed PDF includes executable SAS DATA/PROC REG/PRINCOMP blocks and Stata regressions, but starts from pre-existing datasets such as compu1 and sc_1990 and omits complete imports/producers, Stata data loading and definitions of $control/$pathout.

The full producer-consumer order and input schemas are not supplied for all intermediates; Table 1 has no recipe and online appendix Tables A.1–A.10 have outputs but no workflows. Datasheet-only BEA/DOJ/TRAC source names remain clarification leads. GVKEY.xlsx is only an identifier sheet.

Table 8 consumes log_border, but no border-county ZIP universe, selection steps or log_border producer is supplied. SAS documentation says ZIPCITYDISTANCE uses ZIP centroids and requires SASHELP.ZIPCODE, whose presence/runtime is unverified.
Table 9 consumes an annual firm sheltering probability/top-quartile dummy and references Wilson (2009) through Rego and Wilson (2012), but supplies no estimation recipe, input mapping or producer.
The workflow calls the alternative ETR/CETR analysis Table 6 while the embedded code comment calls it Table 8; intended output/table mapping needs clarification.

evidence.quote: Our sample construction starts with all publicly traded firms with headquarters located in US counties between 1990 and 2012 for which financial data are available from Standard & Poor’s Compustat Annual database.
evidence.description: Compustat Annual is the documented firm-year base for 1990–2012.

evidence.quote: data compu1; set compu1;
evidence.description: Executable SAS DATA-step code is embedded in the PDF.

evidence.quote: output out= compu1_7 R = DTAX ;
evidence.description: The supplied SAS PROC REG block consumes compu1_6 and outputs DTAX.

evidence.quote: proc princomp data = sc_1990 out= sc_1990_1;
evidence.description: The supplied SAS PROC PRINCOMP blocks create social-capital components.

evidence.quote: We hand-collect firms’ historical headquarter addresses by searching headers of electronic 10-K filings from the Securities and Exchange Commission Edgar database.
evidence.description: Historical headquarters are matched to Compustat using CIK and year.

evidence.quote: OLD_NRCRD, reports data for 1990, 1997, and 2005; a new dataset, NEW_NRCRD, reports data for 1997, 2005, and 2009.
evidence.description: The workflow requires both NRCRD versions and the documented years.

evidence.quote: the 1997, 2005, and 2009 Nccs
evidence.description: Documented Nccs estimate, ten-organization Assn harmonization and PCA steps are part of the pipeline.

evidence.quote: We obtain county-level resident age, education, and income data from Census Bureau
evidence.description: The workflow specifies Census county measures and forward-fills missing years.

evidence.quote: We obtain state statutory tax rates are from Council of State Governments Knowledge Center
evidence.description: The CSG Book of the States archive is the stated state-rate source.

evidence.quote: we obtain the annual total number of organ donors in each state in the United States for our sample period, from 1990 to 2012.
evidence.description: The author requires annual state donor counts and state-year per-capita calculation.

evidence.quote: Religious adherence is the fraction of a county’s population that claims affiliation with an organized religion.
evidence.description: Table 4 uses ARDA county religious adherence.

evidence.quote: Corporate irresponsibility equals one if a firm has more than three negative social ratings in a year and it equals zero otherwise.
evidence.description: The dummy is based on negative ratings across seven KLD categories.

evidence.quote: xi: reg ta_etr social_capital $control i.sic2 i.year , cluster (fips)
evidence.description: The PDF contains Stata regression code and outreg2 output commands, with undefined macros.

evidence.quote: All continuous variables are winsorized, at the 1% and the 99% levels using STATA code of winsor2.
evidence.description: The workflow explicitly requires winsor2.

evidence.quote: Table 6 provides additional tests on tax aggressiveness based tax rates
evidence.description: The alternative ETR/CETR code comment in the same block calls the analysis Table 8.

evidence.quote: We use the SAS ZIPCITYDISTANCE function to obtain the distance in miles between a specific company’s headquarter zip code location
evidence.description: The IV analysis needs minimum distance from firm-headquarters ZIP to a U.S.-Canada border county.

evidence.quote: we use the model as reported in Table 5, Column 3 in Wilson [2009] to estimate a tax sheltering probability
evidence.description: This model reference does not supply an executable producer or input mapping for the probability.

evidence.quote: The list of tax haven countries is based on information provided by Dyreng and Lindsay [2009] and Scott Dyreng’s personal webpage
evidence.description: A separate tax-haven jurisdiction list is required for Table 9.

evidence.quote: We define a geographically-diversified firm as a firm that reports material subsidiaries in at least four different states in a given year.
evidence.description: Table 10 uses domestic subsidiary locations by firm-year.

evidence.quote: The data are collected and provided by Dyreng Scott via his personal website
evidence.description: The authors name Dyreng’s Exhibit 21 data as their subsidiary source.

actions.description: Obtain the missing complete author run context before attempting the full pipeline, including ordered producer code, complete input schemas, Stata setup, Table 1 and appendix recipes, and the unresolved derived-input definitions.
steps: Extract the substantial SAS and Stata blocks already embedded in the PDF without normalizing line wraps or continuations; compare each extracted block against the original PDF before use, then request only missing producer/setup context rather than inventing code.
Request all SAS import/producer code and ordered run instructions for raw inputs, compu1, compu1_6/compu1_7, sc_1990/sc_1997/sc_2005/sc_2009, merges and the Stata panel.
Request Stata data-loading instructions and definitions of $control and $pathout, plus the Table 1 summary-statistics procedure.
Request procedures and input crosswalks for online-appendix Tables A.1–A.10; treat datasheet-only BEA/DOJ/TRAC IRS origins as source leads until associated with actual analyses.
Request the exact log_border producer, firm ZIP input, eligible border-county ZIP universe and SASHELP.ZIPCODE version.
Request Wilson/Rego shelter probability variable definitions, inputs and estimation/ranking steps.
Clarify whether the alternative ETR/CETR code block belongs to Table 6 or Table 8.
validation: Confirm every consumed intermediate has a supplied producer and inputs, and documented order covers the main-paper tables and appendix analyses.
Confirm Table 1 and each Table A.1–A.10 result has a recipe and linked data inputs before any authorized run.

review_notes: The embedded SAS and Stata blocks count as supplied executable author code. The PDF is a partial workflow, not a complete runnable program; GVKEY.xlsx is an identifier sheet only. No author code, regression or dataset download was run.

Local catalog candidates and bounded probes do not establish author-version compatibility, full coverage or absent licenses. Appendix-only source names remain workflow clarification leads until mapped to output recipes.
